title: Breach Predictor Request and Support tickets: how they are created and what the Tickets page lists

prose.text: {{support-origin}} The Support ticket system differs between pages {{divergence:support-ticket-system}}. {{support-submit}}
{{integration-required-and}} {{integration-required-or}} The integration requirement is worded differently across pages {{divergence:integration-requirement}}.
Priority and status values are open {{gap:ticket-values}}.

types.statement: Breach Predictor has Request tickets and Support tickets: Request tickets are created from policy recommendations, and the navigation page says Support tickets are created for other improvements that do not involve policy updates; other pages describe Support tickets as covering suggestions, problems with the software, or software bugs.

quotes: Request tickets are created based on the policy recommendations that Breach Predictor provides. Support tickets are created for other improvements that do not involve policy updates.
Additionally, you can use Support tickets to suggest improvements or log software bugs.
Support tickets cover updates that don't involve policy changes (i.e., suggestions or problems with the software).

request-origin.statement: Request tickets are created from the Findings page; Breach Predictor analyzes existing policies (for example File Type Control, SSL Inspection, URL Filtering) and automatically populates the ticket with the threat family, its MITRE ATT&CK placement and the policies that require updates.

quotes: Request tickets are based on Breach Predictor policy update recommendations and are created from the Findings page.

Breach Predictor uses its extensive threat information to analyze your existing policies (i.e., File Type Control, SSL Inspection, URL Filtering, etc.) and suggests policy updates based on that analysis.

Breach Predictor automatically populates the ticket request with specific information about the threat family involved, its placement on the MITRE ATT&CK matrix, and the policies that require updates.

jira-policy-tickets.statement: From the Threat section of Findings, Jira tickets can be created so that Zscaler Support can make policy updates to remediate threats.

quotes: In the Threat section, you can create Jira tickets so that Zscaler Support can make policy updates to remediate the threats affecting your organization.

request-steps.statement: Creating a Request ticket: Update Policy on the Threat page opens the Recommendation panel; Create Ticket opens a panel where the policies to update are selected and a name and details are provided, followed by a Confirm Update window.

quotes: On the Threat page, click Update Policy.
In the Recommendation panel, review the policy recommendations, then click Create Ticket.
select the policies to update, provide a name and details for the ticket, then click Create.
In the Confirm Update window, click Confirm.

support-origin.statement: A Support ticket request is created from the Support tab on the Tickets page, and Zscaler Support uses the information provided to create a ServiceNow ticket as needed.

quotes: You can create a request for a Support ticket directly from the Support tab on the Tickets page, and Zscaler Support uses the information you provide to create a ServiceNow ticket as needed.

support-submit.statement: A Support ticket request is submitted through the Describe your issue field; a Zscaler Support team member follows up with more information and a ticket number if a ticket is created.

quotes: in the Describe your issue field, enter information about the update you're requesting.
A Zscaler Support team member will follow up with more information and a ticket number if a ticket is created.

integration-required-and.statement: Ticket creation requires that Breach Predictor be integrated with Jira and ServiceNow; the Tickets page links to the instance of Jira or ServiceNow in a separate browser tab.

quotes: Ticket creation in Breach Predictor requires that you integrate Breach Predictor with Jira and ServiceNow.
After integration, you can access instances of Jira and ServiceNow where you can see more specific details about each ticket.
The Breach Predictor Tickets page provides high-level details about each ticket, with a link that opens your instance of Jira or ServiceNow in a separate browser tab.

integration-required-or.statement: To see the tickets filed by the organization, Breach Predictor must be integrated with Jira or ServiceNow.

quotes: To see the tickets filed by your organization, you must integrate Breach Predictor with Jira or ServiceNow.

request-columns.statement: The Request tab lists Ticket ID (the Jira number), Priority (assigned by Zscaler Support), Assignee, Created Date, Ticket Name and Status (the current workflow status) for each Request ticket.

quotes: Ticket ID: The Jira number of the Request ticket.
Priority: The ticket priority assigned by Zscaler Support.
Assignee: The person to whom the ticket is currently assigned.
Created Date: The date the ticket was created.
Ticket Name: The unique name of the ticket.
Status: The current workflow status of the ticket.
evidence.after: View details of the Request tickets filed by your organization.

support-columns.statement: The Support tab lists Ticket ID (the Jira number), Requested, Description, Created Date (when Zscaler Support created the ticket) and Status (the current workflow status) for each Support ticket.

quotes: Ticket ID: The Jira number of the Support ticket.
Requested: The date the ticket was requested.
Description: The description of the Support ticket.
Created Date: The date the Support ticket was created by Zscaler Support.
Status: The current workflow status of the ticket.
evidence.after: View details of the Support tickets filed by your organization.

ticket-values.title: Which ticket priority values and workflow status values exist
ticket-values.detail: Both Tickets tabs carry a Status column showing the current workflow status, and the Request tab a Priority assigned by Zscaler Support, but the captured articles list no priority values or workflow status values.

support-ticket-system.summary: The Tickets page labels the Support ticket ID as a Jira number, while the Requesting Updates article and the 2025-02-03 release entry have Support tickets created in ServiceNow.

positions.says: The Support tab's Ticket ID is the Jira number of the Support ticket.

quotes: Ticket ID: The Jira number of the Support ticket.

positions.says: Zscaler Support creates a ServiceNow ticket for a Support ticket request.

quotes: Zscaler Support uses the information you provide to create a ServiceNow ticket as needed.

positions.says: The February 03, 2025 release entry calls them Support (ServiceNow) tickets, against Request (Jira) tickets.

quotes: Additionally, you can create Support (ServiceNow) tickets to report problems and suggest improvements to Breach Predictor.

support-ticket-system.impact: Do not state which system holds a Support ticket, or what its Ticket ID refers to, as settled.

integration-requirement.summary: The captures state the ticketing integration requirement three ways: Jira and ServiceNow for ticket creation, Jira or ServiceNow to see tickets, and Jira and ServiceNow to log tickets for policy changes.

positions.says: Ticket creation requires integrating Breach Predictor with both Jira and ServiceNow.

quotes: Ticket creation in Breach Predictor requires that you integrate Breach Predictor with Jira and ServiceNow.

positions.says: Seeing the organization's tickets requires integrating with Jira or ServiceNow.

quotes: To see the tickets filed by your organization, you must integrate Breach Predictor with Jira or ServiceNow.

positions.says: The navigation page lists Jira and ServiceNow as the integrations used to log tickets for policy changes.

quotes: or with Jira and ServiceNow to log tickets for policy changes.

integration-requirement.impact: Do not state that both systems, or only one, must be integrated as settled; check the integrations on the Profile page's Integration tab.
